contracts.contract_plain_english: For each block-FMA dot product, the paper rewrites every computed term as the exact scalar product times one perturbation from chained output roundings and one from internal arithmetic. Their exact gamma bounds yield (3.4), including the mixed product term; right-to-left blocked summation permits the internal index q+b-1, and equal internal/FMA precision with no coarser final rounding removes the chained-rounding factor entirely. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: displayed factorization, equation (3.4), and following paragraph).

source_evidence.anchor: equations (2.3)-(2.6) and the paragraph defining gamma notation
source_evidence.observation: The paper uses the standard relative-error model, defines gamma_k(v)=kv/(1-kv), assumes kv<1 for relevant k and precisions, and explains that accents and the FMA superscript identify the associated unit roundoff.

source_evidence.anchor: Algorithm 3.1 and the paragraph immediately following it
source_evidence.observation: Algorithm 3.1 partitions the inner dimension into q=n/b blocks, converts operands to u_low if necessary, chains block FMAs with output precision u_FMA, optionally rounds to output precision u, and assumes no underflow or overflow in the analysis.

A dot product is evaluated through block partial sums s_i. Each block expression is evaluated at internal precision bar_u and then rounded according to the effective unit roundoff tilde_u_FMA defined in (3.3), with the first branch taking priority.

source_evidence.anchor: displayed factorization immediately before equation (3.4), equation (3.4), and the paragraph following it
source_evidence.observation: The computed dot product is factored as a sum of x_i y_i times two perturbation factors, with |alpha_i| bounded by tilde_gamma_q^FMA and |beta_i| bounded by bar_gamma_n. Equation (3.4) gives the resulting absolute forward-error bound; the following paragraph gives a sharper right-to-left index and states that (3.4) remains valid for every evaluation order of (3.1).

statement.algorithm_linkage: The contract concerns one scalar entry of the matrix product computed by the chained block-FMA loop on line 6 of Algorithm 3.1. (PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor: Algorithm 3.1; PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.1)).
binders: Let n,b,q be positive integers with q=n/b, so the n scalar products are grouped into q consecutive blocks of length b. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: definition of s_n and equation (3.1)).
Let x=(x_1,...,x_n) be a row of A, y=(y_1,...,y_n) a column of B, and s_n=x^T y=sum_{i=1}^n x_i y_i. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: paragraph introducing x, y, and s_n).
Let s_hat_i denote the computed block partial sums obtained from s_0=0 by (3.1), and let s_hat_n be the final computed dot product. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equations (3.1) and (3.2)).

Let bar_u be the internal block-FMA evaluation unit roundoff, u_FMA the block-FMA output unit roundoff, u the final output unit roundoff, and tilde_u_FMA the effective post-evaluation rounding parameter from (3.3). (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: prose before (3.2) and equation (3.3)).
conclusions: The displayed expansion tracks the first block as (x_1y_1(1+bar_theta_b^(1))+...+x_by_b(1+bar_theta_2^(1))) times prod_{j=2}^q(1+bar_theta_b^(j)) prod_{j=1}^q(1+delta_j), and the final block as (x_{n-b+1}y_{n-b+1}(1+bar_theta_{b+1}^(q))+...+x_ny_n(1+bar_theta_2^(q)))(1+delta_q), with intermediate blocks represented by the intervening ellipsis. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: displayed factorization immediately before (3.4)).

Equivalently, there exist alpha_i and beta_i such that s_hat_n=sum_{i=1}^n x_i y_i(1+alpha_i)(1+beta_i), with |alpha_i|<=tilde_gamma_q^FMA and |beta_i|<=bar_gamma_n for every i. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: final line of the displayed factorization before (3.4)).
|s_n-s_hat_n| <= (tilde_gamma_q^FMA + bar_gamma_n + tilde_gamma_q^FMA bar_gamma_n) |x|^T|y|. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.4)).

For right-to-left evaluation of (3.1), which the paper identifies with blocked summation, bar_gamma_n may be replaced throughout (3.4) by bar_gamma_{q+b-1}. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: paragraph immediately following (3.4)).
The paper states that the unreduced bound (3.4) is valid for every order of evaluation of (3.1). (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: final sentence after equation (3.4)).

As an algebraic same-precision specialization, if u<=u_FMA and bar_u=u_FMA=v, then tilde_u_FMA=0 and (3.4) reduces exactly to |s_n-s_hat_n|<=gamma_n(v)|x|^T|y|; one may take alpha_i=0. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.3), compact factorization, and equation (3.4)).

All matrix absolute values are componentwise, and |L_hat||U_hat| is ordinary matrix multiplication of the componentwise absolute-value matrices. (PDF p. 3, printed C126, anchor: componentwise absolute-value convention; PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: equation (4.7)).
A and b_rhs are the unperturbed data in the backward equation; L_hat, U_hat, and x_hat are computed quantities. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4).
error_notions: Theorem 4.4 is a componentwise backward-error result: the computed x_hat exactly solves a nearby system with the matrix perturbed and the right-hand side unchanged. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4).
The theorem does not give a forward-error bound for x_hat or a normwise relative backward error. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: equation (4.7)).
exceptional_values: The theorem is conditional on the algorithm producing factors and substitution producing a solution; breakdown cases are outside its conclusion. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4).
The triangular-solve result used in the proof assumes a nonsingular triangular coefficient matrix. (PDF p. 12, printed C135, anchor: Lemma 4.2).
Underflow and overflow are excluded in the inherited matrix-update analysis, and NaNs or infinities are not modeled. (PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor: paragraph following Algorithm 3.1).
higher_order_terms: Equation (4.7) retains u_low^2, the mixed gamma product, (1+u_low)^2, and (gamma_n)^2. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: equation (4.7)).

The coefficient in (4.7) is not a dominant-term or big-O approximation; the dominant-term specializations appear only later in Table 4.1. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: equation (4.7) and paragraph introducing Table 4.1).

The inherited Algorithm 3.1 analysis simplifies possible double rounding by retaining one rounding and supplies no explicit remainder for the omitted one. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: double-rounding paragraph before (3.2)).
hypotheses: A is supplied in working precision u and Algorithm 4.1 uses precision u for diagonal block factorization and block triangular solves. (PDF p. 11, printed C134, anchor: section 4 introduction and Algorithm 4.1 lines 2 and 4).
Algorithm 4.1 produces L_hat and U_hat, and subsequent substitution produces x_hat for Ax=b_rhs. (PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: Theorem 4.4).
Trailing updates convert computed factor blocks to u_low and evaluate the update with Algorithm 3.1 and a b_blk x b_blk block FMA. (PDF p. 11, printed C134, anchor: Algorithm 4.1 lines 8-9).
The standard floating-point model holds and k times each relevant unit roundoff is less than one. (PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor: equations (2.3)-(2.4) and gamma definition).

Block update arithmetic contributes tilde_gamma_{q-1}^FMA, bar_gamma_{n-b_blk+1}, and their product, while local block factorization or triangular solves contribute gamma_{b_blk}. (PDF p. 12, printed C135, anchor: Theorem 4.3 and proof; PDF p. 13, printed C136, anchor: equation (4.7)).
